name: Sterling-Nakamura Aegis SMG AS-7 'Wasp Nest'
description: A bullpup submachine gun designed for close-quarters corporate facility defense, firing caseless 4mm rounds from a helical magazine that holds 80 rounds. The AS-7 features an integrated friend-or-foe identification system linked to Sterling-Nakamura's employee biometric database — the weapon physically locks its trigger mechanism if pointed at a registered friendly. This IFF system has been both praised as a safety innovation and condemned as a loyalty enforcement tool, since it means the weapon literally cannot be turned against its issuing corporation.
specifications:
caliber: 4mm caseless
magazine: 80-round helical
rate of fire: 900 RPM
effective range: 5-40 meters
weight: 2.4 kg loaded
IFF system: Biometric trigger lock linked to Sterling-Nakamura employee database
fire modes: Semi, burst, full auto
story_hooks: An AS-7 with its IFF system intact was used to kill a Sterling-Nakamura executive — meaning either the system was defeated or the killer is a registered employee.
A firmware update to the AS-7's IFF database has accidentally flagged hundreds of current employees as hostiles — security teams are finding their own weapons locked out mid-shift.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular bullpup design with an aggressive forward profile. The weapon presents a wedge-like silhouette with the magazine occupying the upper-rear chassis. Its industrial aesthetic suggests precision engineering married to corporate security doctrine—sleek but unapologetically utilitarian.
physical_description.dimensions: 38cm overall length, 8cm width at magazine housing, 12cm height including top-mounted rail system. Barrel length: 16cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Light and well-balanced despite the 80-round helical magazine, sitting comfortably at 2.4kg loaded. The weight distribution favors the shooter's torso, reducing muzzle rise during sustained fire.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel reinforcement at stress points. The helical magazine is machined aluminum with internal polymer followers.
physical_description.finish: Matte black DLC-coated steel components contrasted against charcoal polymer. The helical magazine features a brushed aluminum finish with subtle wear marks from repeated loading cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal black primary with silver-grey accents on the magazine housing and rail systems. Subtle corporate Sterling-Nakamura blue accent striping along the top charging handle.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized pistol grip with aggressive texturing for sweaty-palm security work. The charging handle is wrapped with thin cord binding for positive acquisition.
distinctive_features: Helical magazine with visible round-count witness holes running the length of the upper receiver
Integrated optics rail with factory-standard 20mm mounting points
Biometric sensor array embedded in the trigger guard—small LED indicators (red/green status lights) flush with the polymer
Serrated heat vents along both sides of the forward grip
Minimalist iron sights integrated into the top rail
Ambidextrous fire selector with tactile detents for semi/burst/full positions
Small Sterling-Nakamura corporate shield embossed near the magazine well
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura logo etched on the right-side receiver plate with small serial number below. 'AS-7 WASP NEST' designation stamped in block letters on the magazine housing. IFF system warning label on the left side of the trigger guard.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulous. Security personnel maintain these weapons religiously—expect light holster wear on the grip, minor polymer scuffing, and well-maintained chromium on the barrel. The helical magazine shows consistent wear from insertion cycles. No battle damage; these weapons are rotated out before they degrade significantly.
